title: Functions act on paths: for f from A to B there is an operation from x = y to f(x) = f(y) carrying refl to refl

standard_prerequisites: The identity type of a type A and its reflexivity element refl x.
The induction principle for identity types (path induction) with its conversion rule.
Ordinary (non-dependent) functions f from A to B and the identity type of B.
core_obligations: Construct, by path induction, for every function f from A to B an operation from x = y to f(x) = f(y).
Verify the conversion rule that the operation sends refl x to refl of f(x) by definition.
proof_roadmap: Define the type family D over x, y, p by D(x, y, p) = (f(x) = f(y)): the goal family assigns to each path in A the corresponding equality type in B.
Base case: for each x in A, the element d(x) = refl of f(x) inhabits D(x, x, refl x) = (f(x) = f(x)).
Apply the induction principle: the element J(D, d, x, y, p) inhabits D(x, y, p) for every path p; define the action of f on p to be this element.
Check the conversion requirement: the conversion rule of the induction principle gives that the operation sends refl x to refl of f(x) by definition.
difficulty_reason: A single path induction with a one-line base case; the only care point is that the goal family lands in the identity type of B rather than of A.
